newsitem.title: UK: UK soccer clubs "overvalued by one billion stg".
newsitem.headline: UK soccer clubs "overvalued by one billion stg".

text.p: British soccer clubs, which have increased in value by 400 percent in a year, are "over-hyped and overvalued by up to one billion pounds", accountancy and consulting group Coopers & Lybrand said on Monday.

Based on current share prices, the total market capitalisation of clubs is between 2.0 and 2.5 billion stg, Coopers & Lybrand said in a report. This includes clubs listed on the stock market and an estimate for the private sector.
Experts in Coopers & Lybrand Business Valuation Group say the fundamental value of the soccer sector is nearer 1.5 billion stg.
They say the difference is down to thinly traded shares, a high "emotional' factor attaching to those shares and hype surrounding the potential for Pay-Per-View TV.
"Inevitably there will be a shake-up in the next couple of years and the bubble will burst," said Mark Palios, a Coopers & Lybrand partner specialising in soccer club management.

"This will lead to a dramatic polarisation with a few winners and a lot of losers. Structural change is a certainty both in the game itself and in club ownership," added Palios, himself a former professional player.
The study predicts that only a handful of clubs with strong strategic and financial management can justify their valuations.
